themes.note: Two themes follow the macOS system appearance via <html data-theme>. The frontmatter carries the ink (dark) values, which are also the pre-hydration fallback. Each colorMeta entry carries its paper (light) counterpart in `lightValue`.

accent.purpose: Active tab underline, selected row edge, focus rings, bookmark stars, resizer, drop targets, input focus border, Markdown links, loading pulse. Nowhere else.

accent-strong.purpose: Hover state of an ember element, mainly Markdown links. A state, not a second accent.

bg.purpose: The reading field: preview pane and window ground. The active tab adopts it so the tab joins the content plane.

bg-sidebar.purpose: Recessed chrome: sidebar, tab strip, toolbar, table headers. Darker than the reading field so chrome sits behind the artifact.

bg-elevated.purpose: Detached surfaces: context menu, quick-open panel, address-bar error tip.

bg-row-hover.purpose: Pointer-over state for rows, tabs, and icon buttons.

bg-row-selected.purpose: Selected row, quick-open selection, badge ground, primary sidebar button surface.

border.purpose: Every 1px divider, panel border, table cell edge, and toolbar group separator. Separation is always a hairline.

fg.purpose: Body text and active icon glyphs.

fg-muted.purpose: Secondary text, inactive tab labels, section headers, icon buttons at rest.

fg-dim.purpose: Tertiary text: chevrons, keyboard hints, footer text, resting file glyphs.

fg-path.purpose: Filesystem paths in the retrieval surfaces (start page, quick open) and in file notices. Its own token because a path is what tells two same-named artifacts apart: it must clear 4.5:1 on Raised Ink, Held Ink and Shadowed Ink in BOTH themes, which --fg-dim did not (2.77:1).

heading-fg.purpose: Markdown headings and the start-page wordmark.

label-active-fg.purpose: Label of a selected or hovered file row: the brightest value in the system.

code-bg.purpose: Inline code chip background in rendered Markdown.

code-fg.purpose: Inline code text. Ember-adjacent but weaker, so code does not read as a link.

pre-bg.purpose: Fenced code block ground: the deepest recess in the reading surface.

input-bg.purpose: Address bar field ground. Darker than surrounding chrome so the field reads as a recess.

input-border.purpose: Resting input border, replaced by the accent on focus.

button-hover-bg.purpose: Hover surface of a filled button and the tab close target.

badge-bg.purpose: External-file badge, zoom indicator, keyboard chips, notice strip.

badge-fg.purpose: External-file badge text: the one ember mark that labels rather than marks state.

error-fg.purpose: Failure only: read errors, deleted-file notice, destructive menu items, remove-bookmark hover.

star-idle.purpose: Unbookmarked star at 0.35 opacity until its row is hovered.

scrollbar-thumb.purpose: Scrollbar thumb on a transparent track, 10px wide with a 5px radius.

display.purpose: The start-page wordmark in New York serif. One instance in the whole product.

headline.purpose: Markdown h1 in rendered artifacts, with a 1px bottom rule. h2 follows at 1.5em ruled, h3 at 1.25em unruled.

title.purpose: In-app notice headings, such as the file-deleted state.

body.purpose: The app's own chrome text and the root font size. Tabs and sidebar rows step down to 12px; explorer rows step up to 14px.

reading.purpose: Rendered Markdown body in a 900px measure. The only place where comfort outranks density.

label.purpose: Uppercase section headers at 0.06em tracking. Bookmarks step down to 10px.

mono.purpose: The address bar, every filesystem path, the start-page subtitle, code and preformatted text. Code blocks render at 13.5px.

shadows.name: menu-lift
shadows.purpose: Context menus: a surface that appeared at the pointer and will vanish.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Modal overlays such as quick open, over a rgba(10, 8, 5, 0.4) scrim.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: State feedback: hover, focus, opacity reveal, chevron rotation.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system.

motion.name: start-rise
motion.purpose: Start page entrance: 6px rise with opacity fade, once per mount.

motion.name: tab-pulse
motion.purpose: Loading dot on a tab: opacity 0.25 to 1 and back.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global override. Every animation in the system must survive it.

layoutConstants.name: chrome-band
layoutConstants.purpose: Sidebar drag strip and tab strip: their bottom borders form one line across the window.

layoutConstants.name: sidebar-clamp
layoutConstants.purpose: Resizable sidebar range, dragged by a 6px hit target.

layoutConstants.name: overlay-measure
layoutConstants.purpose: Quick open panel at 12vh, capped at 60vh.

layoutConstants.name: start-measure
layoutConstants.purpose: Start page column with a 56px top inset that clears the traffic lights.

layoutConstants.name: window-min
layoutConstants.purpose: Enforced window minimum. There are no responsive breakpoints.

narrative.overview:
This is not a browser and not an editor. It is the desk of someone who keeps things: a workspace tree that holds a collection, bookmarks and recents that record what mattered, a quick-open palette that retrieves on demand, and a reading surface where the held object is finally examined. Custody comes first, reading second. Every surface in the chrome exists to fetch, hold, or hand over an artifact, and then to get out of the way while it is read.

The material is warm. Neutrals carry a low warm hue in both themes — an ink palette (#1c1a17 upward) after dark, a paper palette (#faf8f4 downward) in daylight — and the two follow the macOS system appearance without a manual switch. A single ember accent is the only chromatic voice in the product. It marks what is active, what is held, and where the keyboard is. Nothing else in the interface is allowed to be colorful.

Density is deliberate. Base UI type is 13px, rows are 30px, chrome bands are 38–40px tall, and the radius scale stops at 10px. The system reads as crafted, archival and patient: built to be lived in for hours by one person who knows every shortcut, not to impress on first sight. Confirmed rejections: cool editor blue-grey, glassmorphism and backdrop blur, neon or high-saturation accents, and rounded consumer-app playfulness.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutrals only; no cool grey anywhere in the chrome.
One accent, used as a marker and never as decoration.
Dual ink/paper themes driven by the OS, with the same structure in both.
High density: 13px UI type, 30px rows, 4px spacing grid.
Native macOS posture: overlay title bar, system fonts, system appearance.
The artifact viewport is the largest and quietest region on screen.

rules.name: The Single Lamp Rule
rules.body: There is one accent hue in the product. If a new element needs to stand out, it earns tone, weight, or position — not a second color. A screen showing more than a few ember marks at once has lost the metaphor.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No neutral in this system is hue-neutral or cool. Every grey carries a warm cast. A #2a2a2a or a #8892a0 anywhere in the chrome is a defect, not a variation.

rules.name: The Coral-Means-Broken Rule
rules.body: Coral is reserved for something that failed or will be destroyed. It never marks emphasis, novelty, or a required field.

rules.name: The One Serif Moment Rule
rules.body: New York appears on the wordmark and nowhere else. A second serif element dilutes the only moment the product speaks in its own voice.

rules.name: The Paths Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a filesystem path renders in mono, dimmed to Ghost Parchment and right-aligned when it trails a filename. A path in the UI font is a defect.

rules.name: The Density Floor Rule
rules.body: Chrome type does not go below 10px, and 11px uppercase labels always carry 0.06em tracking. Small type without tracking is unreadable at this density.

rules.name: The Aligned Band Rule
rules.body: The sidebar's drag strip and the tab strip are both 38px, so their bottom borders form one unbroken line across the window under the traffic lights. Any new top-level chrome band matches that height or explicitly sits below the line.

rules.name: The Artifact Gets the Rest Rule
rules.body: Chrome takes fixed bands; the artifact takes every remaining pixel. No chrome element grows with the window.

rules.name: The Earned Lift Rule
rules.body: Lift responds to detachment or state. A surface that sits in the layout is flat and separated by tone and a 1px rule; a surface that floats above the layout casts a warm shadow. Decorative resting shadows are not part of this system.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadow color is warm-black, never rgba(0,0,0,x). A neutral shadow over warm ink reads as a cool bruise.

rules.name: The 10px Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds a 10px radius. No pills, no capsule buttons, no circular avatars. The desk is made of rectangles.

rules.name: The 2px Marker Rule
rules.body: Selection and activity are marked by a 2px ember bar on an edge. Filling a whole element with the accent is not how this system says "active".

dos: Do define every new color as a theme token in both the :root ink block and the [data-theme="light"] paper block. A hard-coded hex in a component breaks the OS-driven theme switch.
Do mark active and selected state with a 2px ember bar on an edge (::after for tabs, box-shadow: inset for rows).
Do keep the accent to markers: activity, selection, focus, held state, and links.
Do render every filesystem path in mono, dimmed to Ghost Parchment and right-aligned when it trails a filename.
Do hold the 4px spacing grid and the 4/6/10px radius scale.
Do transition on var(--dur-fast) (80ms) for state feedback and var(--dur) (160ms) for larger moves, both on var(--ease).
Do give every interactive element a :focus-visible ember ring, and keep prefers-reduced-motion support intact.
Do reveal icon-only affordances (close, star, remove) on hover of their row, and keep them present when the row is active.
donts: Don't introduce cool grey. No #2a2a2a, no blue-grey editor chrome, no neutral rgba(0,0,0,x) shadows.
Don't add a second accent hue. Ember is the only chromatic voice; coral is failure, not color.
Don't use backdrop-filter, frosted panels, or translucent chrome. Surfaces are opaque and warm.
Don't exceed a 10px radius, and don't build pills, capsules, or circular containers.
Don't put a resting shadow on a surface that sits inside the layout.
Don't add a second serif element; the wordmark owns that voice.
Don't let chrome grow with the window, and don't add responsive breakpoints. The sidebar split is the only elastic axis.
Don't fill an element with the accent to say "selected". Use the 2px marker and a tone step.
